record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Determine the Laurent coefficient bodies for analytic functions taking values of modulus at most unity in a given annulus Ar = {z : r < |z| < 1}. Determine the extremal functions. (M. Heins)

evidence.quote: Determine the Laurent coefficient bodies for analytic functions taking values of modulus at most unity in a given annulus Ar = {z : r < |z| < 1}. Determine the extremal functions. (M. Heins)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix $r\in(0,1)$ and let $A_r=\{z\in\mathbb{C}: r<|z|<1\}$. Let $\mathcal{B}(A_r)$ denote the family of holomorphic functions $f:A_r\to\overline{\mathbb{D}}$ (i.e., $|f(z)|\le 1$ for all $z\in A_r$). Each such $f$ admits a Laurent expansion
$$f(z)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} c_n(f)\, z^n,\qquad z\in A_r.$$
For every finite index set $N=\{n_1,\dots,n_k\}\subset\mathbb{Z}$, define the Laurent coefficient body
$$V_N(r)=\big\{(c_{n_1}(f),\dots,c_{n_k}(f))\in\mathbb{C}^{k}: f\in\mathcal{B}(A_r)\big\}\subset\mathbb{C}^{k}.$$
Problem: Determine the sets $V_N(r)$ explicitly (e.g., describe their boundaries by sharp inequalities), and characterize the extremal functions $f\in\mathcal{B}(A_r)$ whose coefficient vectors lie on $\partial V_N(r)$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published complete determination of the Laurent coefficient bodies for bounded analytic functions on an annulus, nor a full description of the extremal functions. While related extremal problems on multiply connected domains (Pick-type problems studied by Garabedian–Heins, linear extremal problems, Bloch constants) appear in the literature, no source confirms a definitive solution to the general coefficient-body problem in $A_r$. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Linear extremal problems for analytic functions
status_evidence.snippet: General theory of linear extremal problems for analytic functions on planar domains.
status_evidence.claim: Provides general framework for extremal problems but does not give an explicit solution for Laurent coefficient bodies on an annulus.

status_evidence.title: The Bloch constant of bounded analytic functions on a multiply connected domain
status_evidence.snippet: Studies bounded analytic functions on multiply connected domains, motivated by questions of Heins.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses related extremal questions of Heins on annuli, but not the explicit Laurent coefficient bodies.
